findings.frames: 19217 (slider pops in at full size); 19217-19326 slider parked at the bottom; 19326->19327 jump of 313 px; small hops at 19341 (20 px) and 19382 (10 px); after the G->H cut it is parked again 19397-19486; 19486->19487 jump of 215 px; snap at 19548
findings.what_viewer_sees: The yellow zipper slider never slides. It appears at full size in one frame, then sits at the bottom of the seam for 3.6 s while the narration says 'unzips from the bottom up'. At 10:44.23 it teleports about 300 px north. In that same frame half the zipper teeth vanish and the cyan new-ocean strip with its ridge line pops in along the whole lower seam. After the cut it parks mid-seam for another 3 s, then teleports about 215 px to the equatorial end at 10:49.57, together with the yellow 'remaining seam' dot.
findings.evidence: Yellow-pixel centroid tracked with a frame-exact decoder (1920 px coordinates): (801,780) at f19326 -> (950,505) at f19327; (869,575) at f19486 -> (928,368) at f19487. Between these frames it moves only 0.1-1.8 px per frame, which is camera drift. Tiles: every 10th frame from 19217-19327 shows the slider in the same place until 19327. Crops of 19325-19328 and 19484-19489 show the teeth and cyan strip changing in a single frame.
findings.likely_cause: drawZipper puts the slider at integer seam-pair index k, the first pair whose open value is <= 0.5 (ch5a.js:370, :390). open is a per-pair threshold on the plate-rotation gap (seamAt, ch5a.js:108). Long stretches of pairs cross 0.5 in the same frame, so k jumps by dozens of pairs at once. seamUnder's cyan quads (ch5a.js:196) and the H-scene dot (ch5a.js:423) use the same thresholds. The slider is only drawn once k > 0 (ch5a.js:391), so it appears without any scale-in.
findings.suggested_fix: Drive the zipper from a continuous, monotone front instead of the integer k. For example, zipF = mono([[M.zip+0.1,0],[M.split,0.25],[M.firstt,0.6],[M.seam,0.85],[M.snap2-0.05,1]]) and kf = zipF(t)*(n-1). Place the slider at lerp(pts[floor(kf)], pts[ceil(kf)], frac). Draw teeth only for i > kf. In seamUnder for 'satl', fill quads only for i < kf (clip the last quad by frac). Place the yellow dot from kf. Scale the slider in over about 0.2 s with E.outBack instead of popping it in at full size.

findings.what_viewer_sees: During the assembly ('Africa, India'), Madagascar, the pale island between Africa and India in the middle of the frame, disappears in one frame at 10:11.60. Gondwana is then shown without it. At 10:35.40, right after 'Cracks open', a large pale landmass pops into the Africa-India channel in one frame.
findings.evidence: Frame-exact crops: f18347 shows the island and f18348 does not. Block diff 54.5 vs a local median of 6.2. At f19062 the block diff is 78 vs a median of 1.7 at (0.66,0.50), and crops of 19060-19063 show the island appearing. Both flips happen exactly where the counter crosses 170.5 Ma. In ch5a_data.js, the Madagascar polygon (coast_TTT index 631 at 180, 630 at 179-176, 631 at 175, 632 at 174, 631 at 173, 630 at 172-171) is in EXCL for 171-180 Ma but not for 170 Ma and younger. Madagascar (coast_000 polygon 913) is not a member of any tracked plate in work_ch5a/member2.json.
findings.likely_cause: The per-Ma classifier in work_ch5a/export.py (lines 13-23, nearest-point test per Ma with no temporal coherence) wrongly tags Madagascar as part of a tracked plate for Ma >= 171. Paleo.drawBase then skips it (ch5a_paleo.js:76,82), so it toggles on and off at the integer-Ma step. The same mechanism causes smaller flips, for example the NE-Brazil sand sliver at 125.5 Ma (f19449) and a West Antarctic block at 165.5 Ma (f19094).
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the Madagascar indices listed above from EXCL[171..180] so Madagascar is drawn throughout, or regenerate with export.py changed so it never excludes polygons that belong to no tracked plate. Also enforce temporal coherence: a polygon's class must not flip at a single Ma step, and any class change should be faded over +-1 Ma in drawBase.

findings.what_viewer_sees: Throughout the 40-s forward run, the untracked land moves in visible ticks a few times per second while the highlighted plates glide smoothly. This includes Antarctica, the 'keypiece' and centre of frame in 10:33-10:39, plus Madagascar, Arabia and the Asian margin. Antarctica's coastline and the Weddell Sea islands twitch about 4 px every 5-6 frames. In the slam shot, the Asian coast right beside the crumple marks twitches as well.
findings.evidence: Phase correlation on the Antarctica region in scene F gives 0 px for four frames, then (-1,+4) px at f19057, then 0 again. The outlier-block scan shows a spike at every counter tick (f19046/52/57/62/67/73/78). Amplified diff images at f19057, f19190, f19690, f19804, f19911, f20098 and f20128 show bright outlines only on base-land pieces (Antarctica, Madagascar, Arabia, Asia) at the Ma ticks, and faint outlines on the tracked plates. The crop at f19190 shows the Antarctic coast shifting 10-15 px against the smooth cyan seam strip.
findings.likely_cause: Paleo.draw renders all base land, including Antarctica (ANT[Ti] plus antX), from the coast_{round(T)} snapshot (ch5a_paleo.js:93,99). Only the four tracked plates are rotated continuously. At 2-6 Ma/s the snapshot changes every 5-15 frames, and each snapshot is an independent reconstruction, so shapes also change slightly.
findings.suggested_fix: Draw Antarctica like a tracked plate: rotate its present-day rings (coast_000 ANT[0] polygons, already loaded as antPts in ch5a.js:74) by P.rot('antarctica', T) every frame, and drop ANT/antX polygons from the base. For the remaining base land, blend the floor(T) and ceil(T) snapshots: cache both canvases and draw base(Ti0) at alpha 1-f and base(Ti0+1) at alpha f with 'lighter' compositing into a scratch canvas, so pieces glide instead of ticking. Do this for both P2 and P4.

findings.frames: 18503->18504 (detector E3); the slam itself runs 18506-18508 and the flash is at 18509
findings.what_viewer_sees: Five frames before the Gondwana lock, every coastline on the globe swells in one frame. Antarctica's jagged coast and its island clusters turn into smooth blobs, the gaps at the Antarctic Peninsula and the Weddell Sea close, and the white plate rims triple in width. Only then do the pieces slam and flash, so the lock starts with a twitch.
findings.evidence: Mean abs diff of f18504 vs f18503 is 6.73, against 0.1 before. The actual slam frames are 1.8, 2.9 and 3.4, so this is the largest change of the lock apart from the flash. A full-res side-by-side of 18503 and 18504 shows the coast inflation and the closed gaps.
findings.likely_cause: ch5a.js:242 hard-toggles shelf: t > M.gond - 0.2 ? 12 : 0. The shelf adds a 12-px fill-coloured stroke to the base land and every plate (ch5a_paleo.js:87, :125) and widens the white rim from 5.2 to 17.2 px (:124).
findings.suggested_fix: Ramp the shelf with the convergence: shelf: Math.round(12 * prog(t, M.gond - 0.2, M.gond - 0.04, E.in)). Integer steps keep the drawBase cache small. Alternatively, switch it on at t >= M.gond - 0.03, the same frame as the white flash and shake, so the flash masks it.

findings.what_viewer_sees: On 'Then it slams into Asia' the flash, shock rings and crumple zigzags fire, but India never touches Asia. Its northern tip and the zigzags sit in open water, 60-140 px below the Asian coast. India also does not stop at the impact: it keeps creeping north for the next 2 s.
findings.evidence: In the f20130 crop (11:11.00), a dark gulf separates India's tip and the zigzag marks from the pale Asian coast. Computed from tracks.json and the coast data, India's present-day northern tip rotated to 44 Ma is 2.66 deg (about 300 km) from the nearest base land; the gap only drops below 0.5 deg around 20 Ma. Tracking India's top edge gives about 1.5 px/frame before the flash and still about 0.55 px/frame afterwards (364 px at f20117 to 336 px at f20168).
findings.likely_cause: The slam is only a time stamp. The Tfwd key [M.slam, 44] (ch5a.js:120) does not correspond to contact for the present-day India outline, which lacks Greater India. The crumple marks are drawn at India's own tip (ch5a.js:612-618). The mono-cubic still has a slope of about -4.6 Ma/s at M.slam and continues to 38 Ma at tN+0.4, so India keeps moving after the impact.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an India-only pull that closes the measured gap exactly at M.slam: po.explode = { india: -gapDeg * prog(t, tM, M.slam, E.in) }, with center set to a point on the Asian margin just north of contactLL (negative degrees move the plate toward the centre). Anchor the crumple marks on the Asian coast. Stop the clock on impact by replacing [tN + 0.4, 38] with [M.slam + 0.25, 43.5], [tN + 0.4, 43] so India visibly halts on 'slams'.

findings.what_viewer_sees: On 'As they drifted apart', all the continents fly from 180 Ma to today in about 1.1 s right after the dissolve. Almost the whole break-up (145 Ma to 54 Ma) happens in about 0.3 s, so it reads as a jump rather than a drift. The next line, 'they roughly kept their orientation', then plays over a globe that has already stopped, so the orientation claim is never seen in motion.
findings.evidence: The counter reads 161, 145, 120, 86, 54, 31 at 3-frame steps (f20462-20477). Computed T falls up to 11.8 Ma per frame (about 350 Ma/s), compared with 2-6 Ma/s in the forward run. Mean frame diff stays at 8-11 per frame for about 10 frames (f20465-20474).
findings.likely_cause: TO = t => 180 * (1 - prog(t, tO + 0.1, M.apart + 0.55, E.inOut)) is a 1.41-s cubic ramp, compressed further by the 0.45-s dissolve that covers its start. The PLOOK->RLOOK morph (ch5a.js:761) and the TODAY chip follow immediately.
findings.suggested_fix: Stretch the drift through 'orientation', for example prog(t, tO + 0.35, wordAt('s080', /^orientation/i) + 0.6, E.inOutSine), which gives about 3.5 s. Move the look morph and the TODAY chip to after it. Lay the trails down behind the moving tips (trail(name, 180, TO(t))) so viewers watch the points keep their heading while they move.

findings.what_viewer_sees: At the invisible O->P scene boundary, the yellow ripple rings around Antarctica reset: the faint outer ripple vanishes and a new one starts on the ring. The whole globe also shifts and scales by about 1-2 px.
findings.evidence: Mean diff 1.21 at f20682 vs about 0.2 for its neighbours. The amplified diff shows every coastline, the limb, the dotted paths and the droplets moving, plus the ring ripples restarting. A crop tile of 20680-20683 shows the ripple discontinuity.
findings.likely_cause: Scene P restarts the ripple phase: drawRing(..., tP) at ch5a.js:776, while scene O uses M.aim - 0.05 at :766. camP is built with camK, whose time origin k0 = tP restarts withDrift's altitude breathing alt*(1+0.006*sin(0.7*lt)) (shots.js:29), so lt jumps from 7.85 to 0 and the altitude changes by about 0.4 %.
findings.suggested_fix: In scene P call drawRing(ctx, t, 1 - 0.4*sc, M.aim - 0.05). Evaluate camP with the time origin at tO, for example by prepending a key at tO equal to camO's tP state, or by calling camAt(keysRelToTO, t - tO, 0.3), so the drift and breathing phases stay continuous.

findings.frames: 19071-19135 (seam unchanged until about 19130; cyan full at 19135)
findings.what_viewer_sees: 'and new ocean starts seeping in' is heard at 10:35.71-10:37.03, but the seam does not change. The cyan new-ocean strip appears about 1.7-1.9 s later, together with Africa's highlight on the word 'Africa'.
findings.evidence: A tile every 5th frame from 19070-19155 shows no cyan until f19130-19135 (10:37.67-10:37.83). Word timings: 'ocean' at 635.91 and 'Africa' at 637.67.
findings.likely_cause: Both the seamUnder alpha and the new-ocean glow are keyed to M.afant ('Africa'): ga = prog(t, M.afant - 0.15, M.afant + 0.35) and na = env(t, M.afant - 0.1, tG, ...).
findings.suggested_fix: Start the seep on the word 'ocean': const tOcean = wordAt('s075', /^ocean/i); ga = prog(t, tOcean - 0.1, M.afant + 0.35, E.out). Start na at tOcean - 0.1 as well, and keep Africa's highlight (afHL) on 'Africa'.

findings.what_viewer_sees: In the paper textbook figure, 'and their pointy ends all sat close to' plays over a static map. The red tip markers and dashed lines to the ring arrive only on 'Antarctica', about 1.6 s after 'pointy ends'.
findings.evidence: A tile every 6th frame from 20344-20410 shows no tip markers until f20404 (11:20.13). 'pointy' is at 678.35 (f20350) and 'Antarctica.' at 680.11.
findings.likely_cause: The tips are gated on M.ant2: if (t > M.ant2 - 0.12) with a0 = M.ant2 - 0.12 + i*0.1.
findings.suggested_fix: Start the tip markers at wordAt('s079', /^pointy/i) - 0.1 and let the dashed lines grow toward the ring through 'close to Antarctica'. For example, keep the a0 stagger but base it on tPointy, and lengthen the line progress to end at M.ant2 + 0.3.

findings.what_viewer_sees: In the Explorer house gag, a thin dark shadow sliver floats at foot level and runs from his boots across the cabin wall, above the curved ground. The cabin's lower-right corner is sunk about 40 px into the globe surface while its left corner hovers at the limb.
findings.evidence: A full-res crop of f19640 (and f19620) shows the dark streak at shoe height crossing the cabin wall, and the cabin base overlapping the pale Antarctic surface. Every-14th-frame crops 19620-19774 show it throughout the shot.
findings.likely_cause: A flat ShadowMaterial floor disc at y=0 (ch5a.js:462) is seen almost edge-on by the low stage camera (y=0.22) and composited over a 2D globe whose surface curves away (ch5a.js:522). The cabin's pose CAB is fixed in stage space (ch5a.js:477-478) rather than fitted to the projected limb.
findings.suggested_fix: Hide the floor (floor.visible = false) and draw a soft 2D contact-shadow ellipse at (feet.x, feet.y + 2) together with ringE. Raise the cabin (CAB.y about -0.05), or set its rz from the limb tangent at its projected base, so it sits on the curve.

result.intended_notes:
Intended and reading well:
- Hard cuts on the beat, computed from voice markers in ch5a.js:61-63: E1 (chapter start), E5, E6, E7, E9, E12, E15, E16, E18, E19 and E20.
- E2 and E13 are designed punch-in cuts (tA2 'cut in closer for they lock together'; tH on 'first'). They are close to jump cuts, but they are intended.
- E4 lock flash + thunk.
- E6 Bacon outExpo slam-in.
- E8 drip arrows + shake on 'the whole'.
- E10 cracks + shake.
- E14 snap burst. The slider vanishes under it, which is fine.
- E17 porch-light flicker on 'house' (lampOn).
- E21 slam flash, rings and shake. The animation is designed, but see S7-5 for the missing contact.
- E22 and E23 are the designed 0.3 s and 0.45 s dissolves.
- E24 scars headline and stitches.

The only detector events that are defects are E3 (S7-4) and E11 (S7-2).

Clean stretches:
- Chapter card and the RLOOK->PLOOK morph.
- Scene C keypiece lift and slam.
- Bacon insert.
- Drips scene E.
- House-gag character animation: Idle->Wave->Idle_Neutral->Idle crossfades, the 1.667 s Wave loop is seamless, the turn and the lamp, with no T-pose or snaps.
- Paper-figure lock at 11:16-11:17.3.
- Scars ending.

All six chunk starts in the segment (18450, 18900, 19350, 19800, 20250, 20700) are continuous: diffs equal their neighbours and mean signed RGB shift is under 0.2 levels. No ch2_sets-style look change was found.

The GONDWANA title is cut while still about 45 % visible at the E5 hard cut. That is acceptable.

The README audio flags (10:29.5, 11:10.2, 11:32.2) coincide with the impact_deep cues at -10/-8/-6 dB (ch5a.js:336, 624, 787). Audio is out of scope here.

Tooling caveat: tools/grab.py runs ffmpeg without -fps_mode passthrough. For some seek points ffmpeg duplicates the first decoded frame (reported dup=1, e.g. start 19485), so every later tile label is one frame late. All frame numbers in this report were checked with a passthrough decoder. Adding '-fps_mode passthrough' to grab.py fixes it.
